The failing spec is line regulation (0.0537 V/V against a 0.029 V/V limit). Of the candidates, M4 has by far the largest sensitivity (+67% for +20%), so the fault is most likely an oversized M4 in the PMOS mirror. Its drain operating point (Vds = 0.343 V, saturated) and its current ratio to M3 (0.614/0.209 ≈ 2.9) are consistent with the m=3 mirror, so the ratio itself looks intact. Reducing M4's effective size by roughly 15–20% should bring line regulation under the limit. M3 and R1 are the next most plausible contributors.
